Question Choices: Fill: A rectangle has a length of 5 cm and a width of 3 cm. What is the perimeter of the rectangle? (in cm)
Solution: Add all four sides:5+3+5+3=2 x(5+3)=16 linear units.

Question Choices: Select. The perimeter of a square is 20 feet. How long is each side of the square?: ~~2-feet | 4-feet | 5-feet | 10-feet~~
Hints: Divide the square perimeter by 4 to recover one side.
Solution: A square has four equal sides. Divide its 20-foot perimeter by 4:20/4=5 feet. Check:4 x 5=20.

Question Choices: Fill: The perimeter of a rectangular picture frame is 30 inches. The length of the frame is 9 inches. What is the width of the frame? (in inches)
Hints: Subtract both known lengths from the perimeter, then divide the rest by 2.
Solution: Two lengths use 2 x 9=18 inches. Subtract from perimeter:30-18=12. Two widths share that remainder, so each width is 6 inches. Check:2 x(9+6)=30.

Question Choices: Select. A square has a side length of 4 meters. What is the area of the square?: ~~8-square-meters | 12-square-meters | 16-square-meters | 20-square-meters~~
Hints: A square has equal length and width. Multiply the side by itself.
Solution: Area=length x width=4 x 4=16 square units. A square uses its same side for both factors.

Question Choices: Fill: A rectangular sticker is 8 inches long and 2 inches wide. What is the area of the sticker? (in square inches)
Hints: Multiply length by width; area uses square units.
Solution: Area=length x width=8 x 2=16 square units. This counts all unit squares in the rows.

Question Choices: A square has a side length of 6 meters. What is the perimeter of the square? (in meters)
Hints: A square has four equal sides, so multiply one side by 4.
Solution: All four sides equal 6. Perimeter=4 x 6=24 metres.

Question Choices: A rectangle has an area of 8 square centimeters and a perimeter of 12 centimeters. The rectangle is longer than it is wide. What are the length and width? (in cm) Length: ___ cm. Width: ___ cm.
Hints: Find positive side lengths whose product is the area and whose sum is half the perimeter.
Solution: Half the perimeter is 12/2=6, so length+width=6. Their product must be 8. The factor pair 4 and 2 has both properties. Length is the larger:4;width 2. Check:area=4 x 2=8;perimeter=2 x(4+2)=12.

Question Choices: A rectangle has an area of 24 square meters and a perimeter of 22 meters. The rectangle is longer than it is wide. What are the length and width of the rectangle? (in m) Length: ___ m. Width: ___ m.
Hints: Find positive side lengths whose product is the area and whose sum is half the perimeter.
Solution: Half the perimeter is 22/2=11, so length+width=11. Their product must be 24. The factor pair 8 and 3 has both properties. Length is the larger:8;width 3. Check:area=8 x 3=24;perimeter=2 x(8+3)=22.

Question Choices: Select. A vegetable garden is 12 meters long and 5 meters wide. A flower garden is 10 meters long and 7 meters wide. Which garden has a larger area?: ~~vegetable-garden | flower-garden~~
Hints: Calculate both areas separately. Equal perimeter does not force equal area.
Solution: First area=12 x 5=60 square metres. Second area=10 x 7=70 square metres. 70>60, so the flower garden is larger.

Question Choices: Select. A gardener wants to build a rectangular fence around his flower bed. He has 24 meters of fencing. He notices two possible rectangles that both use all the fencing. Rectangle A - 5 m by 7 m. Rectangle B - 3 m by 9 m. He states that both use 24 meters of fencing, so they must have the same area. Is his statement correct?: ~~Yes | No~~
Hints: Calculate both areas separately. Equal perimeter does not force equal area.
Solution: First area=5 x 7=35 square metres. Second area=3 x 9=27 square metres. Both perimeters are 24 metres, but 35!=27; equal perimeter does not mean equal area.
